chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammāt, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the house of Fatimah, with al-Husain sitting on his lap, he began to cry and fell into prostration. Then he said: O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad! Indeed, the Most High, the Most Exalted, appeared to me in this house of yours at this hour in the most beautiful form and appearance. He said to me: O Muhammad, do you love al-Husain? I said: O my Lord, he is the coolness of my eyes, my flower, the fruit of my heart, and the skin between my two eyes. He said to me, O Muhammad, while placing His hand on the head of al-Husain (peace be upon him): Blessed is the newborn upon whom are My blessings, My prayers, My mercy, My pleasure, My blame, My curse, My wrath, My punishment, My disgrace, and My chastisement upon those who kill him, oppose him, contend with him, and compete with him. Indeed, he is the Master of Martyrs from the first to the last in this world and the Hereafter, and the Master of the Youth of Paradise from among all creation. His father is better and more excellent than he is. Convey My greetings to him and give him glad tidings that he is the flag of guidance, the beacon of My friends, My trustee, My witness over My creation, the keeper of My knowledge, and My proof upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earths, and the two weights, the Jinn and the humans.

key_terms.الْعَلِيَّ الْأَعْلَى: The Most High, the Most Exalted (Allah)
key_terms.قُرَّةُ عَيْنِي: Coolness of my eyes (term of deep affection)

ai.seo_question: What did Allah say to Prophet Muhammad regarding al-Husain in the house of Fatimah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the divine validation of Imam al-Husain’s status through a theophanic vision (Tajalli) in Fatimah’s home, linking his martyrdom directly to the Prophet’s love. It establishes him as the 'Master of Martyrs' and a living proof (Hujjah) for all creation, emphasizing his role as a repository of divine knowledge and a beacon of guidance for the faithful.
